vendor: MLflow Project (a Series of LF Projects, LLC / Linux Foundation)
product_family: Open-source, self-hosted AI/ML engineering platform (Apache 2.0): experiment tracking, LLM/agent tracing & observability, evaluation, prompt management, model registry, and an AI Gateway. Originally created by Databricks, donated to the Linux Foundation in 2020. No MLflow-operated hosted SaaS product exists for the core open-source project; third parties (e.g. Databricks, Nebius) separately sell managed-hosting offerings built on top of it.

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type 1/2)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. mlflow.org has no trust center, security page, or compliance page; the project's GitHub security policy covers only vulnerability disclosure and does not mention SOC 2.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of an ISO 27001 certification for the MLflow project.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of an AI-governance certification.

certifications.name: GDPR (posture)
certifications.proof_quote: No MLflow-specific GDPR posture page. The only located privacy document, LF Projects' general privacy policy, covers website/cookie data collection on lfprojects.org and Linux Foundation project sites, not processing of user model/experiment data by the self-hosted software: "describes policies and procedures about the collection, use, disclosure and sharing of personal information when you use their websites... and participate in or use their Project sites."

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a HIPAA compliance statement or BAA offering; no MLflow-operated hosted service exists to sign a BAA for.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not applicable to a self-hosted OSS tracking/observability tool with no payment processing.

privacy.ai_training_note: MLflow is self-hosted infrastructure software, not a hosted AI/ML service: users run MLflow on their own servers/cloud accounts, and their experiment data, traces, prompts, and models never transit an MLflow-operated backend. There is no MLflow entity that could train on customer data because there is no MLflow-run product tier that ingests it. This differs from third-party managed offerings (e.g. Databricks Managed MLflow), which are separate vendor products with their own data-handling terms.
privacy.data_region: User-controlled; self-hosted deployment means data residency is determined entirely by where the customer runs their own MLflow server/infrastructure. No MLflow-operated data centers exist for the core open-source product.

security.name: Encryption in transit / at rest
security.value: Not applicable at the vendor level; self-hosted deployment means encryption is configured and controlled entirely by the customer's own infrastructure (e.g. TLS termination, storage encryption on their chosen backend).

security.name: Vulnerability disclosure
security.value: Managed via GitHub's coordinated/private vulnerability reporting process on the mlflow/mlflow repository; the project explicitly does not accept reports via bug-bounty platforms like Huntr.

security.name: Project governance
security.value: Hosted under the Linux Foundation as "MLflow Project, a Series of LF Projects, LLC" - a vendor-neutral open governance model, Apache 2.0 licensed.

security.name: Known CVE history
security.value: MLflow has had publicly disclosed CVEs in the past (e.g. hard-coded default credentials, auth bypass, path traversal in artifact handling) that were patched via the standard OSS release process; this is normal for widely-used self-hosted OSS and is not a certification gap, but customers self-hosting MLflow are responsible for patching and hardening their own deployment.

products.name: MLflow (Open Source Core)
products.category: Self-hosted ML/LLM/agent tracking, tracing, evaluation, prompt management, and model registry
products.data_scope: Fully self-hosted; customer controls all infrastructure, storage, and data. No data sent to an MLflow-operated backend.

products.name: Databricks Managed MLflow
products.data_scope: Customer data processed within Databricks' hosted platform, subject to Databricks' own compliance program (not MLflow project's).
products.notes: Separate commercial vendor (Databricks, Inc.). SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA certifications for this offering belong to Databricks, not to the MLflow open-source project.

products.name: Nebius Managed Service for MLflow
products.data_scope: Customer data processed within Nebius' cloud, subject to Nebius' own terms/compliance program.
products.notes: Separate commercial vendor (Nebius). Same host-vs-vendor caveat as Databricks Managed MLflow.

compare.pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache 2.0) for the core self-hosted project; paid managed-hosting alternatives are sold separately by third parties (Databricks, Nebius, and others)
compare.data_residency: User-controlled (self-hosted); not applicable to a specific vendor-operated region

flags: MLflow is an open-source, self-hosted project (Apache 2.0, governed by LF Projects, LLC / Linux Foundation), not a commercial SaaS vendor. There is no trust center, SOC2/ISO/HIPAA certification, or DPA for the core open-source software because there is no MLflow-operated service that processes customer data.
Managed/hosted MLflow offerings exist from third parties (notably Databricks Managed MLflow and Nebius). Compliance certifications those hosts hold belong to the host, not to the MLflow project.

The only privacy document found (LF Projects' privacy policy) governs website/cookie data on lfprojects.org and Linux Foundation project sites in general, not the software's handling of user experiment/model data - it should not be read as a data-processing privacy policy for the MLflow product itself.

The maturity taxonomy (enterprise/growth/startup) is a poor fit for a widely-adopted (30M+ downloads/month, Linux Foundation-governed) open-source project with no commercial vendor entity, so maturity is shown as unknown rather than forced into a SaaS-vendor category.
